data.name: Murghib
data.gender_notes: Murghib is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Murghabah' which means 'to attract'. It is a name given to a child who is expected to attract people towards him with his gentle and loving nature. The name Murghib carries the meaning “The One Who Attracts” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Murghib usually hope their child will grow to embody the one who attracts and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a child who is expected to have a gentle and loving soul, and to attract people towards him with his kindness and compassion.
data.etymology: Murghib belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The One Who Attracts.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Murghib total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

This name is associated with the ingrained notion of love, kindness, and compassion towards fellow human beings. It is often compared to the qualities of a well-loved and respected leader who is able to unite and bring people together, creating an environment of peace and unity, as the name suggests, one who attracts people towards him.

It is a name that encourages individuals to radiate positivity and compassion, and to strive to be a source of comfort and solace to those around them. It also serves as a reminder of God's love and compassion towards His creation and the importance of reflecting this love in our interactions with others.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr (Conquest of Egypt), 2/77. The name Murghib carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Murghib ibn Masruq al-Fihri, a Berber chieftain, led a rebellion against the Arab Muslim rule in Egypt. He was defeated and killed by the Muslim general, 'Amr ibn al-'As.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Khaldun, Al-'Ibar, 2/122. The name Murghib carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Murghib ibn Sa'id al-Buzuri, a Marinid Berber ruler, led the invasion of the Maghreb region (North Africa) against the Hafsids. He was eventually defeated and killed by the Hafsid ruler, Abu 'Abd Allah II.
